title: Adaptive Optimize: Safe recommendation apply & rollback playbook for batching and KV cache
creator: Aisha Singh
summary: Follow-up ticket for the incident where an Optimize agent recommendation caused a transient latency spike and partial error rate increase. Deliver a playbook that formalizes safe preflight checks, staged apply procedures, deterministic rollback triggers, and post-apply telemetry guards for batching and KV cache recommendations.
postmortem_summary: On 2026-02-02 an Optimize agent recommendation increased batch sizes and enabled an aggressive KV cache policy for a subset of hosted traffic. Within 12 minutes we observed a 1.8x P95 latency regression and a 2.4% increase in inference 5xx errors for a small customer cohort. Root cause: a model-mixed workload with high variance in sequence lengths combined with a kernel selection path that under-optimized small-batch tail latency. The recommendation lacked a staged canary, insufficient preflight simulation, and had no automated fast rollback criteria. Immediate mitigation was a manual rollback and emergency throttle of the recommendation engine. This ticket captures lessons, mitigations, and an operational playbook to prevent recurrence.
mitigations: Require simulated preflight runs against representative traffic snapshots before any recommendation is applied to production
Enforce mandatory canary windows: 5 minutes small-cohort, 30 minutes expanded cohort before global apply

Introduce three automated rollback triggers: (1) P95 latency increase >20% over baseline sustained 3+ minutes, (2) error rate increase >1% absolute sustained 2+ minutes, (3) CPU/GPU queue depth crossing emergency threshold for 60s
Add a soft-throttle policy that reduces apply rate when any node reports degraded kernel performance metrics
Ship a visibility dashboard that surfaces candidate changes, simulated delta in cost/latency, and the exact binary config diff
Limit maximum single-change surface area: only one parameter family (batch_size or kv_policy) can change in a single apply
Require code-owner approval for applies that affect >5% of traffic or more than 1 model family
Persist deterministic artifacts from the preflight run (trace, token distribution, kernel selection histogram) for postmortem audits
playbook_steps: Step 0 - Preflight: Run the recommendation algorithm against a stored 'representative_snapshot' traffic trace. Produce aggregated simulated P50/P95/P99, token distribution, kernel-path counts, and estimated cost delta.

Step 1 - Safety gates: Validate simulated P95 does not regress >10% and simulated error delta is <=0.2% absolute. Confirm kernel-path distribution does not introduce new unsupported fast-paths for >2% of tokens.

Step 2 - Canary apply (small cohort): Apply to 0.5% traffic for 5 minutes. Monitor P50/P95, error rate, GPU queue depth, and maximum latency tail outliers. Automated canary agent calculates a 'health_score' every 30s.
Step 3 - Canary hold & inspect: If health_score remains >=0.95 for 5 minutes, expand to 5% traffic for 30 minutes. Otherwise trigger automated rollback with annotated reason.
Step 4 - Expansion: After 30m stable at 5%, expand to 25% for 1 hour and run additional integration checks (billing/cost regression validation, routing fallbacks exercise).
Step 5 - Global apply: If expansion window shows no triggers, schedule a global apply during low-traffic maintenance window. Log change, owner, and expected rollback window (1 hour post-apply).
Step 6 - Post-apply watch: Post-apply automated checks run for 60 minutes with tighter thresholds; any trigger causes an immediate rollback and incident alert to on-call SRE and Optimize owners.

Step 7 - Rollback execution: Automated rollback re-applies previous stable config and routes affected traffic away from nodes with anomalous kernel metrics. Notify on-call channel and open a postmortem stub automatically.

Step 8 - Postmortem & improvements: After rollback, collect persistent artifacts from preflight and production traces. Annotate root cause and add needed follow-ups in the ticketing board. Update the recommender model or simulation harness as required.
automated_checks_and_thresholds: Latency P95 delta: auto-rollback if >20% sustained for 3 minutes; alert if >10% sustained for 5 minutes
Error rate delta: auto-rollback if absolute increase >1.0% sustained for 2 minutes; page on >0.5% sustained for 10 minutes
GPU queue depth: auto-throttle if queue depth crosses 85% of configured emergency threshold for 60s
Kernel evictions: alert if kernel-path miss ratio increases >5% relative to preflight simulation
Cost delta guardrail: if cost increases >15% without proportional latency improvement, abort expansion and require PM sign-off
observability_and_reporting: Preflight artifacts bucket: gs://redwood-optimize/preflights/ (persisted traces with timestamps and diffs)
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Build preflight simulator extractor that pulls representative traces and runs the recommender offline. Add simulated metrics output contract
Phase 2 (1 week): Implement automated canary apply workflow with cohort management and health_score calculation. Integrate initial auto-rollback triggers
Phase 3 (1 week): Wire observability: dashboard tiles, alerting rules, and artifact persistence. Add PR that surfaces binary config diffs in the console
Phase 4 (1 week): Hardening: limit change surface area, require code-owner approvals for high-impact recommendations, and add cost delta guardrail
Phase 5 (ongoing): Run tabletop drills quarterly and refine thresholds based on controlled ramp experiments
outstanding_risks: Simulated preflight may not capture rare high-variance traffic bursts leading to false negative safety checks
Too-conservative thresholds might prevent legitimate cost savings; we need a path for fast-experiments with human oversight
Rollbacks may not be instantaneous for distributed cached state; some nodes might continue to serve degraded config until warmed
Complex multi-model deployments (model families with different tokenization) increase difficulty of representative snapshots

acceptance_criteria: Automated preflight simulator produces reproducible P50/P95/P99 and kernel-path histograms for any candidate recommendation
Canary engine can apply and expand cohorts automatically with health_score evaluation and automated rollback on triggers
Observability dashboard displays preflight vs. canary vs. baseline metrics and persists artifacts for audits
Playbook runbook is published to Confluence and linked from the Console when a recommendation is proposed
At least two tabletop drills completed and thresholds tuned based on empirical canary runs
notes: Design request: keep diff UI focused on 'what changed' (parameter name, before/after, estimated impact) and hide low-level binary blobs
Consider a 'fast-path' waiver process for low-latency sensitive customers who want manual review before any automated recommendation
We should record the exact recommender model version and random seed used for simulated preflight to ensure reproducibility
Track cost savings vs. number of rollbacks quarterly to measure net value of automated recommendations
